# Pricing the Inevitable

*Everyone dies. The premium is about when.*

and across
1,000](reference/figures/quote-desk.png)](https://soodpratham10.shinyapps.io/pricing-the-inevitable/)

## You’re at the quote desk

A 40-year-old walks in and asks for \$250,000 of whole life insurance.
The net premium is **\$2,109.46 a year**. That number is a break-even
*on average*, and it hides a bet: at that price the policy still loses
money **one time in three**, because everyone who dies early is a loss.

How much should you charge to be 95% sure of not losing money?

| Policies sharing the risk | Premium for 95% confidence | Above the net premium |
|---------------------------|----------------------------|-----------------------|
| 1                         | \$6,589.87                 | +212.4%               |
| 100                       | \$2,401.47                 | +13.8%                |
| 1,000                     | \$2,200.39                 | +4.3%                 |
| 10,000                    | \$2,138.08                 | +1.4%                 |
| 100,000                   | \$2,118.50                 | +0.4%                 |

That table is why insurance works. This project builds the engine behind
it from first principles, for 19 insurance and annuity products, and
puts it on a desk you can use.

## The Quote Desk

**[The Quote
Desk](https://soodpratham10.shinyapps.io/pricing-the-inevitable/)** is a
Shiny pricing desk in the style of a 1950s insurance office:

- 🖋 **The quote letter**: choose an applicant (age, underwriting class),
  a plan and a payment frequency; the desk types up a quote with the
  premium, the chance of a claim, the chance the policy loses money and
  the premium needed for 95% confidence. Print it, or file it in the
  session’s quote book.
- 🎲 **Risk Lab**: four premium principles side by side, the probability
  of loss as the premium rises, and 1,000 simulated portfolios checking
  the normal approximation.
- ⏳ **Mortality Lab**: Makeham, Gompertz, de Moivre, constant force and
  Weibull, and three ways of spreading deaths within a year.
- 🗄 **Product Shelf**: all 19 products for any age, with the full
  distribution of each one’s present value.
- ⚖ **Natural Hedge**: the mix of annuities and life insurance that
  cancels a mortality shock.
- 🔖 **Beat the Underwriter**: guess the premium for a random applicant
  and get stamped APPROVED, REFERRED or DECLINED.

**[How the desk works
→](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/docs/the-quote-desk.md)**

## What the project found

| Finding | Numbers |
|----|----|
| A net premium breaks even only on average | Whole life at 40 loses money with probability 33.8% at its net premium of \$2,109.46 |
| Pooling makes certainty cheap | 95% confidence costs +212% for one policy and +4.3% across 1,000 |
| A percentile premium alone can give cover away | For 20-year term at 40 the 95% percentile premium is **\$0**, because death within 20 years has probability 4.2% |
| Smokers pay less for annuities | The deferred annuity from 65 costs smokers 18% less: they are expected to collect it for fewer years |
| A flat extra hits term insurance hardest | +0.005 on the force of mortality multiplies 10-year term at 40 by 5.5, but whole life by only 1.46 |
| Paying monthly costs about 2% more a year | The insurer waits for its money and stops collecting at death |
| Insurance and annuities hedge each other | 0.26 annuities of \$20,000 a year per \$250,000 policy cut the effect of a 10% mortality shock from \$1.59 million to \$15,855 |

## The chapters

| Chapter | The story | Actuarial content | Code |
|----|----|----|----|
| 1\. [**The Clock**](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/docs/chapters/01-the-clock.md) | How long will they live? | Laws of mortality, select mortality, extra risk, fractional ages | `R/mortality.R` |
| 2\. [**Paying at Death**](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/docs/chapters/02-paying-at-death.md) | Insurance | Eight insurance benefits: EPV, variance, full distribution, identities | `R/products.R` |
| 3\. [**Paying for Life**](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/docs/chapters/03-paying-for-life.md) | Annuities | Eleven annuities; m-thly by exact sums, UDD and Woolhouse; benefits at the moment of death | `R/products.R`, `R/frequency.R` |
| 4\. [**The Quote**](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/docs/chapters/04-the-quote.md) | Premiums | Equivalence, percentile, portfolio percentile, premium refunds, the rate book, the natural hedge | `R/premiums.R`, `R/ratebook.R`, `R/hedge.R` |

## How it’s built

``` mermaid
flowchart TB
    PKG["R package: inevitable<br/>40 functions, 120 tests"] -->|"every push"| CI["GitHub Actions<br/>R CMD check"]
    PKG --> DB["SQLite<br/>rate book, 50,000 policies, quote log"]
    PKG --> MEMO["Quarto<br/>pricing memo, HTML and PDF"]
    PKG --> APP["Shiny<br/>The Quote Desk"]
    PKG <-->|"matches to the cent"| XL["Excel<br/>rate calculator"]
    PKG <-->|"20 of 20 values"| PY["Python<br/>independent port"]
```

| Tool | Its job |
|----|----|
| **R package** | The engine, `inevitable`: 40 documented functions, 120 tests, checked by GitHub Actions on every push |
| **SQL (SQLite)** | The back end of a quoting system: plans, classes, a 424-rate rate book, 50,000 simulated policies with actual vs expected losses, a quote log, and views an agent would read |
| **Excel** | A working rate calculator with dropdowns, its own life table in formulas, a lookup in the R rate book and a 10-item cross-check |
| **Quarto** | [A pricing memo](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/report/pricing-memo.pdf) to a (fictional) pricing committee, every number computed live |
| **Python** | An independent numpy port of the engine that reproduces 20 key results from R |
| **Shiny** | [The Quote Desk](https://soodpratham10.shinyapps.io/pricing-the-inevitable/) |

## How correctness is checked

- **Hand calculations**: a three-year life worked on paper (q = 0.1,
  0.2, 1 at 10%) for insurance, annuities, premiums and premium refunds.
- **Identities**: A = 1 − d ä; endowment = term + pure endowment;
  increasing + decreasing term = (n + 1) × term; Var(Y) = Var(Z)/d²; the
  UDD m-thly formula equals the exact UDD sum; key relations between
  deferred, guaranteed and term annuities.
- **Independent rebuilds**: Excel to the cent, Python to 1e-14, SQL
  against the model’s probabilities of loss.
- **Automation**: `R CMD check` with every test on every push ([see the
  runs](https://github.com/soodpratham10/pricing-the-inevitable/actions)).

## Try the engine

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("soodpratham10/pricing-the-inevitable")
library(inevitable)

m <- mortality_law()                                   # the project's Gompertz-Makeham law
q <- class_q_path(m, 40, "Smoker")                     # a newly underwritten 40-year-old smoker
net_premium("term", q, i = 0.045, S = 250000, n = 20, t = 20)
portfolio_premium("whole_life", q_path(m, 40), 0.045, S = 250000, N = 1000)
natural_hedge(m)$ratio
```

More in **[Getting
started](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/docs/getting-started.md)**.

## About

Built by **Pratham Sood**, Actuarial Mathematics and Statistics,
University of Manitoba. The idea grew out of a life contingencies course
assignment that valued standard insurances and annuities. This project
rebuilds it from scratch with its own assumptions, and goes further:
full loss distributions, risk-based premiums, underwriting, the natural
hedge, and a tested R package.

Companion projects: [The Odds of a
Lifetime](https://github.com/soodpratham10/odds-of-a-lifetime) (an
insurer over 20 years) and [Matching the
Promise](https://github.com/soodpratham10/matching-the-promise) (the
assets behind an annuity block).

*All assumptions are illustrative and not calibrated to real data. Net
premiums only: no expenses or profit. Nothing here is a real offer of
insurance.*

# Package index

## Chapter 1: The Clock

Laws of mortality, select mortality, extra risk and fractional ages.

- [`mortality_law()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/mortality_law.md)
  : Create a law of mortality
- [`mu_x()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/mu_x.md)
  : Force of mortality
- [`tpx()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/tpx.md)
  : Survival probability under a law of mortality
- [`q_path()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/q_path.md)
  : Annual death probabilities for a life aged x
- [`kpx_from_q()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/kpx_from_q.md)
  : Survival probabilities from annual death probabilities
- [`curtate_pmf()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/curtate_pmf.md)
  : Probability function of the curtate future lifetime
- [`curtate_ex()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/curtate_ex.md)
  : Curtate life expectancy
- [`spx()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/spx.md)
  : Fractional-age survival within one year
- [`tpx_frac()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/tpx_frac.md)
  : Survival to a non-integer time
- [`life_table()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/life_table.md)
  : A life table built from a law of mortality

## Chapters 2 and 3: Paying at Death and Paying for Life

Nineteen insurance and annuity products, with their full distributions.

- [`products()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/products.md)
  : The product shelf
- [`annuity_certain()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/annuity_certain.md)
  : Annuity-certain values
- [`pv_by_k()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/pv_by_k.md)
  : Present value of a product for each curtate lifetime
- [`product_moments()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/product_moments.md)
  : Expected value, variance and distribution of a product's present
  value
- [`epv()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/epv.md)
  : Expected present value of a product
- [`nEx()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/nEx.md)
  : Pure endowment factor nEx
- [`value_all()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/value_all.md)
  : Every product valued at once

## Paying more often than once a year

m-thly and continuous benefits by exact sums, UDD, Woolhouse and claims
acceleration.

- [`nominal_rates()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/nominal_rates.md)
  : Nominal rates of interest and discount
- [`annuity_due()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/annuity_due.md)
  : Life annuity-due on the yearly grid
- [`annuity_due_mthly()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/annuity_due_mthly.md)
  : Life annuity-due paid m times a year
- [`insurance_mthly()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/insurance_mthly.md)
  : Term or whole life insurance paid at the end of the 1/m-th of a year
  of death
- [`insurance_continuous()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/insurance_continuous.md)
  : Insurance paid at the moment of death
- [`insurance_continuous_exact()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/insurance_continuous_exact.md)
  : Insurance paid at the moment of death, exact under a law of
  mortality

## Chapter 4: The Quote

Premium principles and the loss at issue.

- [`net_premium()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/net_premium.md)
  : Net annual premium by the equivalence principle
- [`net_premium_mthly()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/net_premium_mthly.md)
  : Net premium paid m times a year
- [`loss_distribution()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/loss_distribution.md)
  : Loss at issue for every curtate lifetime
- [`prob_loss()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/prob_loss.md)
  : Probability the policy makes a loss
- [`loss_moments()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/loss_moments.md)
  : Mean and variance of the loss at issue
- [`percentile_premium()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/percentile_premium.md)
  : Percentile premium
- [`portfolio_premium()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/portfolio_premium.md)
  : Portfolio percentile premium
- [`simulate_portfolio()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/simulate_portfolio.md)
  : Simulate portfolios to check the probability of a portfolio loss
- [`refund_premium()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/refund_premium.md)
  : Premium for a policy that refunds the premiums on death

## The rate book

Plans, underwriting classes and premiums per 1,000.

- [`risk_classes()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/risk_classes.md)
  : The underwriting classes
- [`class_q_path()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/class_q_path.md)
  : Death probabilities for an underwriting class
- [`plans()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/plans.md)
  : The plans in the rate book
- [`plan_premium()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/plan_premium.md)
  : Premium for one plan
- [`rate_book()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/rate_book.md)
  : The rate book

## The natural hedge

Life insurance and annuities offsetting each other.

- [`shock_q()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/shock_q.md)
  : Shock annual death probabilities
- [`natural_hedge()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/natural_hedge.md)
  : The natural hedge between life insurance and annuities
- [`block_change()`](https://soodpratham10.github.io/pricing-the-inevitable/reference/block_change.md)
  : Change in the value of a hedged block after a mortality shock
